title: Workflows: research, review panel and parallel attempts
bridge: A dynamic workflow is like Promise.all over several agent calls, written as a small script. Except: it runs inside the ticket's own VM. Its agents use the tools of the session that started it, and none of them writes the change. One writer per change stays the rule, even when attempts run in parallel.
intro: Extra agents help most where reading beats writing: research, review and comparing attempts. This lesson covers the spike that proves the Workflow tool works in our VM. Then two saved workflows, research and a review panel. Then parallel build attempts where tests pick the winner. In every piece, one writer per change still holds.

picture.caption: Workflows fan out inside one VM and return one result. Only one change ever ships.

sections.h: The spike, part 1: the session options
p: Start with a real question: does the Workflow tool work headless, in a lite VM, behind our gateway? Headless means no person at a terminal to approve anything. The SDK reference documents the tool, so the question is our setup, not the language. A spike is a half-day throw-away experiment that answers it.

The script runs with npx tsx on a lite VM from the ai-agent-sandbox image. It uses the harness's own settings: the pinned claude binary, the gateway as ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, and permissionMode dontAsk. dontAsk refuses any tool that is not in allowedTools. No Anthropic key is in the VM.
sections.because: Research, plans with a judge, and the review panel all depend on this tool working in our VM.

notes.text: The /core entry, as the bundled harness uses (lesson g3-9). HookCallback and Options are the SDK's types.
A PostToolUse hook on the Workflow tool. It prints the tool's response, which holds the runId.
"user" is added so saved workflows in ~/.claude/workflows/ of the VM user load by name.
The same allowedTools as G3-19, including Workflow. The ticket says: try once without it to see the refusal.
enableWorkflows turns the tool on. workflowSizeGuideline is advice to the model, not a cap. The ticket passes settings as a JSON string; lesson p8-7 passes an object. Both work (see the tip).
The pinned binary the nightly image smoke-tested, so the spike runs what Nova runs.
Resume after a kill: set RESUME_SESSION_ID. resumeFromRunId then works inside that session.
env replaces process.env entirely, so the spread keeps PATH and HOME.
A G0-13 run token for the ticket SPIKE-1. The gateway tags the spend by ticket from it.
The cap on parallel agents: 3 on lite (4 vCPU), 6 on full, 12 on wide.
No maxTurns, no maxBudgetUsd, no taskBudget. Limits never cut a run in the middle.

callout.text: settings takes either form. In the SDK types, Options.settings is a string (a file path or a JSON string) or a Settings object. G4-01 uses JSON.stringify(...), lesson p8-7 uses a plain object, and both are right. Pick one per codebase and keep it.

sections.h: The spike, part 2: run it, kill it, resume it
p: The default prompt asks for a small workflow: three parallel Haiku readers each list five files, then merge. The result message shows the subtype, the cost and modelUsage. Every workflow agent call must show up there and at the gateway with the step header.

Then the checks from the ticket: does the session wait for the workflow (if not, try CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=0)? Does the CPU cap hold? Can a workflow agent start a new run (it must not: no orchestrator access, and workflow() nests one level only)? Does a saved workflow load by name? Does resume return cached agent calls?
The output is a one-page note in ai-agents/docs/spikes/workflows-in-the-vm.md with a go or no-go for the research workflow and the panel.
sections.because: We write down what works and what does not before two tickets are built on top of it.

notes.text: The prompt comes from the command line, so the saved-workflow check is one argument away.
A small workflow on purpose: three cheap readers and a merge. Enough to see parallel agents and the cap.
query() returns an async iterator of messages. We only print the final result.
subtype says how it ended; total_cost_usd and modelUsage show every model the workflow used.

sections.ifInstead: If the session exits before the workflow finishes, set CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=0 so it waits with no ceiling. Note it in the spike page.

sections.h: Research, part 1: the saved workflow and its questions
p: A saved workflow is a plain JavaScript file in ~/.claude/workflows/ of the VM user, baked in by Packer. It starts with export const meta: a name, a description and phases. Nova calls the Workflow tool with the name and args; the tool runs the script.

The research workflow asks four questions in parallel: the code, similar merged PRs, the tests that cover it, and the brain. Each helper returns file:line pointers in a fixed JSON Schema shape. Plain JSON Schema here, not zod, because the script runs inside the tool.

Research runs while Nova plans, before any person approves the plan, so no code may be written yet. The helpers return pointers, never edits, and Nova reads one short list. That keeps one writer per change.
sections.because: Research is where extra agents help most: parallel helpers give the planner a wider view for little cost.

notes.text: meta is what the tool reads to list and load the workflow by name.
Three phases. The tool shows progress per phase, and each agent call names its phase.
The helpers' answer shape: a list of { where, why }. where is a file:line pointer.
Question 1: where is the code. Most relevant first.
Question 2 uses gh through the broker, read-only, for up to 5 merged PRs in the same area.
Question 4 uses the kb skill once G6 ships. Until then the helper says "skipped" and moves on.

sections.h: Research, part 2: three plans and a judge for fuzzy tickets
p: phase() marks a stage. parallel() takes a list of functions that each return an agent call and runs them together, bounded by the CPU cap. agent() runs one helper with a prompt and options: a schema for its answer, a model, an effort.

For a ticket readiness called fuzzy, three planners write a plan each from a different angle. The schema is passed in as args.planSchema, which is z.toJSONSchema(Plan) from lesson g4-2, so each plan has the real Plan shape. A judge picks one and grafts the best ideas from the others.

Nova decides when to run this, guided by one line in plan-and-grill: bigger or fuzzy ticket, research first. The plan says why and roughly how big. The harness never forces it. It stays only if pass@1 on 5 TICKET-BENCH tasks holds or rises.
sections.because: For fuzzy work, independent plans with a judge beat one plan polished on its own.

code.text:
phase('Research')
const found = await parallel(QUESTIONS.map((q) => () =>
  agent(`${q}\n\nTicket:\n${args.ticket}`, { schema: POINTERS, model: 'haiku', effort: 'medium', phase: 'Research' })))
const notes = found.filter(Boolean).flatMap((r) => r.pointers)
if (!args.fuzzy) return { notes }

phase('Plans')
const ANGLES = ['the smallest safe change', 'risk first: what could break', 'the user first: every screen state']
const plans = await parallel(ANGLES.map((angle) => () =>
  agent(`Write a plan for this ticket, thinking ${angle}.\nTicket:\n${args.ticket}\nNotes:\n${JSON.stringify(notes)}`,
    { schema: args.planSchema, phase: 'Plans' })))

phase('Judge')
const plan = await agent(
  `Pick the plan a reviewer and a tester would trust most; graft good ideas from the others. Return the final plan.\n${JSON.stringify(plans.filter(Boolean))}`,
  { schema: args.planSchema, effort: 'medium', phase: 'Judge' })
return { notes, plan }

notes.text: The first phase begins. Everything until the next phase() is reported under Research.
parallel() over the four questions. Each entry is a function, so nothing starts before parallel() decides.
Helpers run on Haiku 5.5 at medium. Each prompt stays under 100K tokens.
A helper that failed returns nothing; filter(Boolean) drops it. The pointers are flattened into one list.
Not fuzzy: return the notes and stop. The planner uses them.
The three angles: smallest safe change, risk first, user first.
Each planner gets the ticket and the notes, and must answer in the Plan schema from args.
The judge inherits the main loop's model, Opus 5.5, at medium. It picks one plan and grafts ideas.
The tool's answer: the notes and the chosen plan.

sections.h: The review panel, part 1: lenses and the skeptic's shape
p: On a large diff one reviewer misses things. A panel runs several lenses in parallel, then a skeptic per important finding tries to refute it. A finding the skeptic cannot refute at file:line survives; the rest are dropped. That finds more and cries wolf less.

The panel runs from the read-only reviewer session of lesson g4-4 (Read, Grep, Glob and Workflow), not from Nova's. Workflow agents use their session's tools, so the lenses and skeptics cannot edit anything. The harness writes the diff to /run/nova/review/diff.patch first.
sections.because: A skeptic per finding is what turns more reviewers into fewer false alarms instead of more noise.

notes.text: The name Nova's reviewer session passes to the Workflow tool.
The lens answer shape: the same fields as the Finding schema in review.ts, as JSON Schema.
The skeptic's answer: refuted or not, and the evidence it found.
Five lenses, one agent each: correctness, security, conventions, plan coverage and tests.
The conventions lens runs on Sonnet 5.5 at low; the others inherit Opus 5.5.
Plan coverage: is every plan item and QA check done? Only the panel checks this against the plan.
Tests: do they read what the user sees, and could they fail? The QA plan rule, applied to the diff.

sections.h: The review panel, part 2: pipeline, and when to fan out
p: pipeline() takes a list and a chain of steps. Each lens runs as the first step; its findings feed the second step, which fans out a skeptic per important finding. A skeptic must show the problem at file:line, or the finding is dropped.

When to fan out is written for G8's plan-and-grill skill. Use the panel for diffs over about 300 changed lines, 8 or more files, or a risky area. Use one reviewer otherwise. Workflow size small (under 5 agents per step) by default. The VM's CPUs bound how many agents run at once.
The panel is tried on the 5 big TICKET-BENCH cases. It stays only if it finds real issues the single reviewer missed, without more false alarms.
sections.because: On small diffs a panel only adds cost, so Nova needs a clear sense of when it is worth it.

notes.text: pipeline(list, step1, step2): each lens flows through both steps.
Step 1: one agent per lens reads the diff file through that lens, with the ticket for context.
lens.opts spreads the model and effort override for the conventions lens.
Step 2: for each important finding of that lens, a skeptic runs in parallel.
A refuted finding becomes null. A surviving one keeps the skeptic's evidence.
Flatten the per-lens lists and drop the nulls: what survived.
log() shows up in the tool's progress. One line, useful in the trace.
The tool's answer: the surviving findings, in the same shape reviewOnce returns.

sections.h: Parallel attempts, part 1: child workflows on their own branches
p: Some tickets are hard: the plan marks them so, or an attempt already failed. For those, the workflow runs 2 or 3 independent build attempts in separate full VMs. Anthropic's SWE-bench score rose from 77.2% to 82.0% with tests picking one of several attempts.

This block lives in ticketToPr, so it is workflow code: deterministic, no Node APIs. Each attempt is a child workflow, buildAttempt, with its own workflow ID and its own branch. One writer per change still holds: each attempt writes only its branch, and only one branch survives.

Each attempt takes a Nova slot (3 at start), so attempts wait in the queue instead of starving other tickets. The default is 2 while the pool is small. All attempts share the ticket's cost tag and backstop.
sections.because: Several attempts with tests picking one raise the pass rate on hard tickets, without breaking one writer per change.

notes.text: executeChild starts a child workflow and waits for its result, all recorded in the parent's history.
act is G3-29's proxied activities with the LONG preset: a safety net, never a work limit.
keepOnlyBranch is a short activity: delete the losing branches through the broker.
n defaults to 2. Branches are nova/RH-1234-a1 and nova/RH-1234-a2.
Promise.allSettled: one failed attempt does not fail the ticket. All children run together.
Workflow ID nova:RH-1234:a1. Each child claims a Nova slot and its own fresh full VM.
Every attempt builds from the same approved plan and the same locked checks.

sections.h: Parallel attempts, part 2: survivors, a judge, one winner
p: An attempt survives only if the locked QA checks pass and the verify command passes. If none survive, the requester gets the best attempt's evidence and the run stops there. With one survivor, it wins. With more, a judge chooses.

The judge is Opus 5.5 at medium. It sees the ticket, the surviving diffs and their check results, side by side. Not the transcripts. It picks one and says why. The other branches are deleted and their VMs released; only the winner goes on to self-review, the PR and Byte.
This is a stretch ticket. It is measured on the 5 big and the hardest TICKET-BENCH tasks first. It stays only if pass@1 rises enough to pay for the extra VMs.
sections.because: Tests, not opinions, drop the bad attempts; the judge only chooses among attempts that already pass.

notes.text: A type guard keeps only fulfilled results, so TypeScript knows r.value exists.
The two gates: the locked QA checks and the verify command. Both must pass.
No survivor: send the requester the best attempt's evidence. A person decides what next.
One survivor wins without a judge call.
judgeAttempts is an activity: a model call with the ticket and the summaries (diffs plus check results).
Delete the losing branches. One change ships; nothing half-done is left on the remote.
The winner's result goes back to ticketToPr for self-review and the PR.

callout.text: One writer per change. Research helpers, planners, lenses and skeptics only read and return data; each attempt writes only its own branch, and one change ships. Nothing inside a VM can start a run: attempts are child workflows the orchestrator starts, each with a Nova slot.

quiz.q: Where does a dynamic workflow run?

options.text: On the orchestrator, as a Temporal child workflow
options.why: That is the attempts block. Research and the panel run through the Workflow tool inside the ticket's VM.

options.text: Inside the ticket's VM, through the Workflow tool, bounded by the VM's CPUs
options.why: The cap is 3 on lite, 6 on full, 12 on wide. Every call goes through the gateway with the run token.

options.text: On a separate wide VM reserved for workflows
options.why: One fresh VM per run. A workflow shares its ticket's VM and backstop.

quiz.q: What makes the review panel find more without more false alarms?

options.why: More findings alone is more noise. The gain comes from the skeptic who must show each problem.

options.text: A skeptic per important finding that must show the problem at file:line or the finding is dropped
options.why: Refuting is the filter. What survives has evidence attached.

options.text: Running the lenses on Opus at high effort
options.why: Effort does not change the structure. The conventions lens even runs on Sonnet at low.

quiz.q: Two parallel attempts both pass the locked checks and verify. What happens next?

options.text: Both PRs open and the reviewer picks one
options.why: Only one change ships. People never see two PRs for one ticket.

options.text: The first one wins, because it finished first
options.why: Order is not a quality signal. A judge compares the survivors.

options.text: A judge sees the ticket, the diffs and the check results, picks one, and the other branch is deleted
options.why: judgeAttempts chooses among passing attempts; keepOnlyBranch removes the rest.

words.plain: A short throw-away experiment that answers one question and ends with a written go or no-go.
Running with no person at a terminal, so nothing can wait for someone to press approve.
A workflow script in ~/.claude/workflows/ that the tool can run by name.
An agent that tries to refute one finding; a finding it cannot refute at file:line survives.
A Temporal workflow started by another workflow, with its own ID and history.
One independent build of the same plan on its own branch and VM; tests and a judge pick one.
An attempt that passes every locked QA check and the verify command.
